sections.label: Global graduate student mental health study
sections.summary: A 2018 global study found 41% of graduate students had moderate to severe anxiety and 39% depression signs.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A global study conducted in 2018 found that 41% of graduate students worldwide suffered from moderate to severe anxiety, while 39% showed signs of moderate to severe depression.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This survey which was based on the responses of over 2,000 students from 230 institutions across 26 countries reported that in general, graduate students are more than six times as likely to experience anxiety and depression compared to the general population.

sections.label: Singapore graduate student living costs
sections.summary: Rising Singapore living costs stress graduate students, especially overseas students, as PhD scholarships provide modest stipends.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Among graduate students, and especially for students from overseas who have come to Singapore to pursue their graduate research, the rising cost of living in Singapore is probably one of the greatest stress factors today.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many PhD students in Singapore are on research scholarships, which provide a relatively modest stipend compared to the salaries that their peers in the workforce may be getting.

sections.label: NUS mental healthcare campaign
sections.summary: The National University of Singapore has run a #AreuOK mental healthcare campaign since 2021.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As an encouraging example of what is already being done, the National University of Singapore has been running a #AreuOK mental healthcare campaign since 2021.

sections.label: National mental well-being campaign
sections.summary: The Health Promotion Board runs the national campaign "It's OKAY to Reach Out" to normalise mental health and encourage support-seeking.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the national level, the Health Promotion Board runs our national mental well-being campaign, "It's OKAY to Reach Out", which seeks to normalise the topic of mental health and well-being, generate greater understanding and awareness and encourage Singaporeans to reach out for support.

sections.label: Economic cost of anxiety and depression
sections.summary: WHO reported depression and anxiety cost the global economy over $1 trillion yearly; a Singapore study estimated almost $16 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The World Health Organization recently reported that depression and anxiety disorders cost the global economy over $1 trillion every year.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another recent study by the Duke-NUS Medical School and the Institute of Mental Health estimated the total economic burden of lost productivity due to anxiety and depression in Singapore to be almost $16 billion annually.

sections.label: Healthcare facilities and worker recruitment
sections.summary: The main challenge for long-term healthcare needs is recruiting, retaining and raising productivity of healthcare workers, not building facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Post-COVID-19, I am hopeful that progress on constructing new facilities like the Woodlands Health Campus and the Integrated Care Hub at Tan Tock Seng Hospital is picking up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the main impediment – the main challenge – in meeting our long-term healthcare needs lies not in the building of physical facilities, it lies in the recruitment and retention and raising the productivity of our healthcare workers.

sections.label: Nurses' pay increase
sections.summary: Nurses' pay was increased last year, the first base salary increase in seven years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While nurses' pay was increased last year – and this is welcome – this was the first base salary increase in seven years.

sections.label: Benchmarking healthcare compensation
sections.summary: The speaker asks if healthcare personnel compensation could be monitored, benchmarked against other developed countries, and published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Many countries would like to poach our English-speaking and well-trained healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask if compensation for healthcare personnel could be monitored and tracked based on hourly compensation – total pay per hour worked – and regularly benchmarked against other developed country locations against which we compete for healthcare talent, with the results published so that we have a clear indicator of how we are doing and whether or not we will face choppy waters ahead that we would need to take heed of.

sections.label: Nursing student intake rise
sections.summary: Minister Ong said the annual intake of nursing students will rise from 2,100 to 2,300 a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister Ong has said that the annual intake of nursing students will rise from 2,100 to 2,300 a year.

sections.label: Singapore Core and nursing careers
sections.summary: The passage states it is important to maintain a strong Singapore Core and career progression for nurses, and notes nursing scholarships by healthcare clusters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is important for such a critical profession to maintain a strong Singapore Core and good career progression for nurses who can progress into more senior nurse practitioner and leadership roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I know that there are currently nursing scholarships primarily awarded by the healthcare clusters.

sections.label: Pharmacist prescribing powers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government will consider giving pharmacists powers to prescribe drugs for certain conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To raise the productivity of our whole system, will the Government consider giving pharmacists some powers to prescribe drugs for certain conditions?

sections.label: Fewer health screenings
sections.summary: The National Population Health Survey 2021 showed fewer Singapore residents participated in chronic disease and cancer screenings in 2021 than 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moreover, alarmingly, the National Population Health Survey 2021 showed that fewer Singapore residents participated in chronic disease and cancer screenings in 2021, compared to 2019.

sections.label: Deploying health coaches in community
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether health coaches, once sufficient in number, can be deployed to void decks, hawker centres and wet markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, I wonder if, once we have the health coaches in sufficient numbers, we can, as one initiative, deploy them to void decks, hawker centres and wet markets.

sections.label: NTU survey of 300 GPs
sections.summary: An NTU survey of 300 GPs found many planned to leave, take a break or reduce hours, citing remuneration, specialty recognition and litigious pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In a survey of 300 GPs by NTU published in the journal BMC Primary Care in 2022, 14.4% said they plan to leave general practice permanently, 12.6% plan to take a career break, and 51.3% plan to reduce their clinical hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Higher remuneration, recognising general practice and family medicine as a medical specialty, and reducing the litigious pressures on medical practice were rated as the most important factors in these decisions, while there was growing dissatisfaction within this community with the third-party administrators that manage insurance arrangements.

sections.label: Private providers tapping ALPS procurement
sections.summary: The speaker understands the Government is studying letting private healthcare providers tap ALPS and hopes it moves soon on combined purchasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Anyway, I understand that the Government is currently studying the idea of allowing private healthcare providers to tap on the Government drug procurement system, or ALPS, and I hope the Government will move on this soon to enable combined purchasing across the public and private sectors to the fullest extent practicable.

sections.label: Accenture study on health workforce technology
sections.summary: A 2019 Accenture study concluded technology could free up time for doctors, pharmacists, nurses, laboratory scientists, pharmacy technicians and medical records clerks in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, a 2019 Accenture study on Singapore's health workforce concluded that technology could free up 10% of time for doctors, 10% for pharmacists, 22% for nurses, 31% for laboratory scientists, 50% for pharmacy technicians and a whopping 68% for medical records clerks in Singapore.

sections.label: AI to augment mental healthcare capacity
sections.summary: Noting Singapore's lagging psychologist and psychiatrist ratio, the speaker asks if AI can augment mental healthcare capacity and suggests working with local companies like Holmusk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our ratio of clinical psychologists and psychiatrists lags behind some other developed countries, a subject that I and other Members have raised previously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Government explore using AI technology to augment capacity in mental healthcare?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore-based company Holmusk has partnered the UK's NHS and Liverpool University to establish a mental health analytics and research hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will consider working with companies like this, particularly locally based ones, to push the envelope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But our future is also one where there will be greater opportunities to exploit technology and innovation to increase efficiency; and to enhance prevention upstream.

sections.label: COVID-19 support for healthcare workers
sections.summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Singapore Government gave healthcare workers financial assistance, resources and training to manage increasing demands while treating patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Singapore Government provided the healthcare workers with vital support in the form of financial assistance, resources and training to help them manage their increasing demands while treating COVID-19 patients.

sections.label: Public health investment and subsidies
sections.summary: The Government has invested significantly in public health infrastructure and subsidised medical care so Singaporeans can receive adequate medical attention regardless of financial background.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has invested significantly in public health infrastructure and subsidised medical care, making it possible for Singaporeans to receive adequate medical attention when required, regardless of their financial background.

sections.label: MOH and SkillsFuture courses for seniors
sections.summary: It would be good if MOH can work with SkillsFuture to increase access and adoption of courses suitable for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For this purpose, it will be good if MOH can work with SkillsFuture to increase the access and adoption of courses which are suitable for our seniors.

sections.label: Improving communication for impaired patients
sections.summary: Healthcare providers may improve communications for the visual and hearing impaired by training staff in sign language or providing communication aids.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition to existing efforts, healthcare providers may improve communications for the visual and hearing impaired by ensuring that their staff is trained in sign language or providing communication aids such as hearing aids or visual aids.

sections.label: Elite athletes access to resources
sections.summary: Elite athletes need access to resources to help them cope with these pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Elite athletes need access to resources to help them cope with these pressures.

sections.label: Teaching exercise and health education
sections.summary: It would be good if MOH, MOE and SportSG teach Singaporeans at a tertiary level how to exercise when they enter the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: He was still young and his tragic and sudden death ignited conversations amongst my peers about being healthy versus being fit, as well as our general education on health and well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would be good if MOH and the Ministry of Education (MOE) together with SportSG teach Singaporeans at a tertiary level how to exercise when Singaporeans enter the workforce.

sections.label: Training staff to de-escalate abuse
sections.summary: Healthcare facilities can train staff to de-escalate tense situations and implement policies for reporting and addressing verbal abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Healthcare facilities can provide training for their staff to de-escalate tense situations and implement policies for reporting and addressing verbal abuse.

sections.label: Investing in medical worker safety
sections.summary: The Government should invest in health and safety measures to protect medical workers from future pandemics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our Government should also invest in health and safety measures to protect medical workers from future pandemics.

sections.label: Mental health screenings in schools
sections.summary: MOE has refreshed the youth curriculum covering well-being, and the speaker hopes mental health screenings are added to regular physical health screening.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am glad that MOE has refreshed our youths' curriculum that covers physical, mental and emotional well-being.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But I hope we can impact mental health more directly, go beyond education or awareness and include mental health screenings as part of our regular physical health screening.

sections.label: Mental health access and professionals
sections.summary: MOH has increased mental health access points via polyclinics and telehealth, but trained professionals are short, so the speaker hopes the profession is regulated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Additionally, it is important to create a supportive and welcoming environment so that they can feel comfortable and feel safe to seek help without any shame or judgement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I am glad that MOH has increased the number of access points via the polyclinics and telehealth services, making mental health services more widely available to people in need.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, I am aware of the shortage of trained mental health professionals who can provide effective and evidence-based treatment for those seeking help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This, too, can lead to inadequate or harmful treatment, worsening the individual's mental health and overall well-being.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, we must continually review our mental health infrastructure, I hope we regulate this profession.

sections.label: Protecting healthcare workers from abuse
sections.summary: The authorities will take a zero-tolerance approach and act against individuals who harass or abuse healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We not only must create a safe and supportive environment for our healthcare workers but enact clear guidelines to protect them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, I am grateful that the authorities will take a zero-tolerance approach and will take appropriate actions against individuals who harass or abuse our healthcare workers.

sections.label: Obesity as M3 focus area
sections.summary: A fifth M3 focus area was announced, with the Healthy Investment programme aiming to mobilise the community for Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our community's obesity rate is the highest compared to the other groups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As we are aware, obesity can lead to health problems like heart disease, diabetes, and high blood pressure, among others.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Therefore, Minister had announced the establishment of a fifth focus area for M3 so that it counts as one of our community’s priorities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This new focus area, through the Healthy Investment programme under M3, aims to mobilise our community to be ready for the Healthier SG programme.

sections.label: Gracious users of healthcare
sections.summary: Given Singapore's highly ranked healthcare system, users should aspire to be ranked among the most gracious in healthcare systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Considering that Singapore’s healthcare system is ranked amongst the best in the world, I think it is time for the users of our Singapore healthcare system, that is patients, families, visitors, all of us to aspire to be ranked amongst the “most gracious” in healthcare systems.

sections.label: Healthier SG incentives and penalties
sections.summary: Healthier SG will incentivise positive behaviours and disincentivise or penalise poor healthcare lifestyles and behaviours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As part of the Healthier SG, the system will incentivise positive behaviours, and poor healthcare lifestyles and behaviours should be disincentivised or penalised.

sections.label: GP as group Advisor
sections.summary: Each GP can be Advisor to a few groups, checking in, advising on activities or joining in, similar to MPs in a constituency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Each general practitioner (GP) can be Advisor to a few groups to check in with them, to advise on activities or even join in, similar to what Members of Parliament do in a constituency.

sections.label: Healthier SG participation credits
sections.summary: With Healthier SG, credits for participation could be used for healthcare or healthy staples like oats and milk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Maybe with Healthier SG, where you have credits for participation and these can be used for healthcare or purchase of healthy staples like oats, milk and so on.

sections.label: Sing Out Loud inter-generational programme
sections.summary: Sing Out Loud! is an Esplanade community engagement programme with Dementia Singapore from 2016, first time involving an inter-generational group.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sing Out Loud! or 大声唱 is a community engagement programme by Esplanade, developed in partnership with Dementia Singapore in 2016, but this is the first time involving an inter-generational group.

sections.label: Hospital staffing challenge
sections.summary: Minister Ong has shared that the key challenge in hospitals is sufficient nurses, allied health professionals and support care staff.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Minister Ong has shared often enough that the key challenge in our hospitals is to have sufficient nurses, allied health professionals and support care staff to operate hospitals, clinics and eldercare centres.

sections.label: Nurses' pay review
sections.summary: Nurses' pay is also being reviewed and implemented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (b) nurses' pay is also being reviewed and implemented which is great.

sections.label: Retired nurses returning to workforce
sections.summary: Retired or part-time nurses may return, but the Singapore Nursing Board stopped registration for nurses not practising over five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This may attract also retired nurses or part-time nurses to return to the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand from the Singapore Nursing Association that there is already a "return back to nursing" scheme for those who left for family reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand, however, that the Singapore Nursing Board has stopped registration for previously-registered nurses who have not been practising in the field for more than five years.

sections.label: Conditional registration for overseas physiotherapists
sections.summary: MOH could consider conditional registration for overseas qualified physiotherapists and allied health workers while they take continuous learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps, MOH can consider conditional registration for these overseas qualified physiotherapists and allied health workers, while they take up continuous learning in the subjects that might not have been part of their training overseas.

sections.label: New capitation funding model
sections.summary: The new capitation funding model must be designed to incentivise and disincentivise behaviours at all care levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The new capitation funding model will play a key part and it needs to be designed to incentivise as well as disincentivise behaviours at all levels of care, including the GPs and the population.

sections.label: Diabetic population budget results
sections.summary: Investing an additional 4% of budget for the diabetic population decreased hospital admits by 22% and other avoidable visits by 21%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For their diabetic population, they invested additional 4% of budget in this group and achieved a decrease in hospital admits by 22% and a decrease of 21% for other avoidable visits and admissions, resulting in overall improvement in value of care and reducing overall costs over time.

sections.label: Home medical care in continuum
sections.summary: Home medical care must play a key part in the continuum of care, with domiciliary services like post-delivery nurse visits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For a sustainable healthcare system, home medical care must play a key part in the continuum of care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A doctor friend shared that there was a scheme at one time, which has since been pulled back, where post-delivery patients could go home because there were nurses visiting baby and mom for three days after discharge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This would be the kind of domiciliary services needed as we transition to a right care at the right time in the right setting, often at home.

sections.label: Uberised certified healthcare professionals
sections.summary: Uberised certified healthcare professionals who schedule their own rosters and work their neighbourhood could be best.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: Perhaps, some form of uberised certified healthcare professionals who schedule their own rosters and probably work the "beat" in their neighbourhood could be the best.

sections.label: Singapore health index ranking
sections.summary: The Legatum Prosperity Index 2023 ranked Singapore first with a health index score of 86.9.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: The latest Legatum Prosperity Index 2023 ranked Singapore in number one position with a health index score of 86.9.

sections.label: Healthcare worker abuse prevalence
sections.summary: Over two in three healthcare workers witnessed or experienced abuse or harassment in the past year, and a third at least weekly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More than two in three healthcare workers had witnesses or experienced abuse or harassment in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A third of all healthcare workers had witnessed or experienced abuse or harassment at least once a week.

sections.label: Frontline workers face abuse
sections.summary: The work group found frontline healthcare workers like pharmacists, patient service associates and nurses more likely to face abuse, commonly shouting, demeaning comments and threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The work group found that that frontline healthcare workers like pharmacists, patient service associates and nurses are more likely to face abuse and harassment, with the most common type of abuse being shouting, making demeaning comments and threatening to file complaints or to take legal action against the healthcare workers.

sections.label: Threats led to resignation
sections.summary: Dr Tan Yia Swam shared an anecdote of a healthcare friend so affected by threats that she had resigned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just this morning, Dr Tan Yia Swam shared with me an anecdote of how one of her friends in healthcare was so affected by threats that she had resigned.

sections.label: Consequences for abusive patients
sections.summary: The work group recommended clear consequences for perpetrators, with abusive patients possibly warned and discharged if not needing urgent attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, one of the work group's recommendations was to stipulate clear consequences for perpetrators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For patients who are abusive, warnings may be issued and they may be discharged if they do not require urgent attention.

sections.label: Zero-tolerance and prosecution support
sections.summary: National healthcare groups will support and implement the recommendations including a zero-tolerance policy, and authorities should prosecute severe abuse cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our national healthcare groups have already said that they will support and implement the recommendations, including a zero-tolerance policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Authorities should also be prepared to prosecute such cases of abuse if they are beyond a certain threshold of severity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that the guidelines that will be issued in the second half of this year will see a sharp reduction in incidence of abuse against our healthcare workers and that it will give them peace of mind as they go to work every day.

sections.label: MediShield Life social insurance
sections.summary: Adverse selection leads to inadequate private insurance, so the Government provides MediShield Life with a public mandate, coverage of pre-existing conditions and subsidies for low-income residents.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The result is that there is an inadequate provision of private insurance.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, in the presence of an adverse selection problem, there is a role for the Government to intervene by providing social insurance in the form of MediShield Life, which was introduced in November 2015.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, there is a public mandate so that all Singapore citizens and permanent residents are included in the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, pre-existing medical conditions are covered, although there are additional premiums for serious pre-existing medical conditions that require intensive medical intervention to treat or require prolonged treatment.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, the Government provides subsidies to low-income residents to help them make their premium payments.

sections.label: Health and social care integration
sections.summary: Care integration needs better organisation, particularly cross-collaboration between health and social care under MOH and MSF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, we need to better organise care integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I agree with Dr Tan Yia Swam that greater cross-collaboration is necessary but I wish to add that this is particularly pertinent between health and social care, which falls under the purview of MOH (MOH) and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) respectively.

sections.label: Ministry of Ageing proposal
sections.summary: It asks whether to move away from an interagency ministerial committee and consider establishing a Ministry of Ageing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Is it time to move away from an interagency ministerial committee and consider establishing a Ministry of Ageing?

sections.label: Healthcare legacy IT systems
sections.summary: Addressing healthcare legacy IT and IT systems used by different clusters is needed to achieve this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To achieve this we need to address the current issue of healthcare legacy IT as well as IT systems being used by different clusters.

sections.label: Health booklet for seniors
sections.summary: One possible solution is giving seniors and caregivers a health booklet with relevant information to help them manage their health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One possible solution is to provide seniors and caregivers with a health booklet containing relevant information to help them manage their health effectively.

sections.label: Seamless care around seniors
sections.summary: The system should seamlessly integrate care services around the senior with a 360 view across acute, long-term, primary and community care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For me, it is a system where there will be a seamless integration of care services organised around the senior, with a 360 view of his physical, mental and emotional health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This will require drawing up care in a seamless manner across settings between acute and long-term care, between acute and primary care and between primary and care in the community.

sections.label: Health and social care integration
sections.summary: Health and social care must transcend boundaries, with information flowing seamlessly and one record, IT system and Ministry of Ageing for integrated care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Health and social care must transcend boundaries to help seniors to age well in the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It will also mean that information should flow seamlessly between hospitals to care professionals in the community to better manage seniors health and social conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The eventual end state would be one patient, one health record or wellness record, one IT system and hopefully all these overseen by one Ministry of Ageing, to deliver coordinated holistic and integrated care to transform Singapore into the best place to live in.

sections.label: Singapore ageing society numbers
sections.summary: Singapore is one of the fastest-ageing societies globally, with one in four Singaporeans a senior by 2030 and every other by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Singapore is one of the fastest-ageing societies globally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We know the numbers very well: one in four Singaporeans a senior by 2030, and every other Singaporean a senior by 2050.

sections.label: National sports participation rise
sections.summary: National regular sports participation rose by some 20%, from 54% in 2015 to 74% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As such, national regular sports participation has risen by some 20%, from 54% in 2015 to 74% in 2022, last year.

sections.label: Active Health Labs islandwide
sections.summary: Eight Active Health Labs have been set up islandwide at ActiveSG sport centres and Active Health partner premises.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Beyond the Health District, we have today set up some eight Active Health Labs island wide, at our ActiveSG sport centres and Active Health partner premises.

sections.label: Sports participation survey well-being
sections.summary: In the 2022 National Sports Participation Survey, 95% said well-being improved through sport and 94% said quality of life improved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Based on the 2022 National Sports Participation Survey, when participating with others, 95% of respondents indicated that their well-being has improved through sport and physical activity; and 94% of respondents indicated participation in physical activity has improved their quality of life.

sections.label: GPs refer community activities
sections.summary: SportSG will work with MOH and HPB to engage GPs to refer clients to community-based activities to improve or maintain health.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Beyond physical activity, SportSG will continue to work with MOH and HPB to engage general practitioners (GPs) to refer clients to suitable community-based activities that can help them improve or maintain their health, as well as understand their fitness and health status.

sections.label: Active Health initiative and labs
sections.summary: SportSG launched Active Health in 2017 to inspire Singaporeans to take ownership of their health and foster community spirit, with eight Active Health Labs island-wide.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: SportSG launched the Active Health initiative in 2017 to inspire Singaporeans to take ownership of their own health, and to foster greater community spirit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Queenstown Healthcare District pilot is a good example.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In addition, we have set up eight Active Health Labs island-wide, at our ActiveSG sport centres and Active Health partner premises.

sections.label: Wish to participate in debate
sections.summary: The speaker states he wishes to participate in this debate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yes, Mr Deputy Speaker, I wish to participate in this debate.

sections.label: Singapore hospital bed count low
sections.summary: Singapore maintains a little more than two hospital beds per 1,000 population, lower than OECD, Japan, South Korea, China, Denmark, the Netherlands, Israel and the United States.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The average of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), an association of industrialised nations, is closer to a dozen, twice our number.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: More generally, our hospital bed count is also low.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: We maintain a little more than two beds per 1,000 of our population, a fraction of that of other East Asian economies, like Japan and South Korea which have around a dozen; China, which has around five; and other advanced economies like Denmark, the Netherlands, Israel and the United States, where the ratio is closer to three.

sections.label: Hospital bed occupancy rates breached
sections.summary: Recent data show the 80% bed occupancy rate is systematically breached, routinely exceeding 90% at Tan Tock Seng, Ng Teng Fong and Khoo Teck Puat hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Moreover, recent data on bed occupancy rates at our major hospitals reveal that this 80% appears to be systematically breached, and over the past month, the rate has routinely exceeded even 90% in Tan Tock Seng, Ng Teng Fong and Khoo Teck Puat hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Taken together, these suggest that the Government is both aware that running our medical infrastructure too lean can come back to bite us during periods of stress, and that we have yet to fully address this problem even though we are back in normal times.

sections.label: Singapore physicians per 1,000 people
sections.summary: As of 2021, Singapore has 2.7 physicians per 1,000 people, around two-thirds the OECD average of 3.8.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: As of 2021, Singapore has 2.7 physicians per 1,000 people, around two-thirds the OECD average of 3.8.

sections.label: Global nurse shortage estimates
sections.summary: The Government says ramping up medically-trained staff is a priority, amid a global nurse shortage estimated by WHO at close to six million.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The Government has stressed the same, that ramping up medically-trained staff is a priority.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: There is a global nurse shortage which the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates may be close to six million and the International Council of Nurses – to be fair, an interested party – places this at a higher number of around 13 million.

sections.label: Waits exceeding 24 hours
sections.summary: On certain days, waits could exceed 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: On certain days, this could lead to waits even exceeding 24 hours.

sections.label: Increasing recognised universities for medical degrees
sections.summary: The speaker suggested considering increasing the number of recognised universities for basic medical degrees from the present 100.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: In my earlier speech, I offered some medium-term suggestions for how we could relieve some of the existing pressure on our system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: We could consider increasing the number of recognised universities for basic medical degrees, up from the present 100.

sections.label: MOE student well-being approach
sections.summary: MOE takes a holistic approach to promoting students' overall well-being and health from when they start school.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: MOE takes a holistic approach towards promoting the overall well-being and health of our students from the time they start going to school.

sections.label: Healthy Meals in Schools Programme
sections.summary: With HPB, all schools implemented the Healthy Meals in Schools Programme, and polytechnics and ITE join HPB's Healthier Dining Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In collaboration with HPB, all schools have implemented the Healthy Meals in Schools Programme, where school canteens provide healthier food and drink options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Similarly, polytechnics and ITE participate in HPB's Healthier Dining Programme, which encourages food operators to offer healthier choices.

sections.label: Schools equip students for mental well-being
sections.summary: Schools and IHLs equip students with knowledge and skills to strengthen mental well-being, build resilience and thrive amidst challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Our schools and IHLs equip students with knowledge and skills to strengthen their mental well-being, build resilience and thrive amidst challenges.

sections.label: Community mental health teams established
sections.summary: Under the Community Mental Health Masterplan, MOH, the Agency for Integrated Care and social service agencies established community mental health teams across Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For example, under the Community Mental Health Masterplan, MOH, the Agency for Integrated Care and social service agencies have worked together to establish community mental health teams across Singapore.

sections.label: Mental well-being advisory and junior doctors' hours
sections.summary: A 2020 tripartite advisory supports workplace mental well-being, and MOM is reviewing junior doctors' total working hours, including on-call hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Advisory on Mental Well-being at Workplaces was jointly launched in 2020 by MOM, the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF) to support employees' mental well-being and provide resources for employers, employees and self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Ministry is reviewing the total working hours of junior doctors, including hours worked while on call.

sections.label: Task force preliminary recommendations consultation
sections.summary: The task force identified 12 preliminary recommendations and sought public views in a consultation process last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: At the task force, we have identified 12 preliminary recommendations and sought the public's views in a consultation process last year.

sections.label: First-stop mental health touch points
sections.summary: One task force recommendation is to designate a few first-stop touch points giving individuals easy access to mental health support and advice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: One recommendation from the task force is to designate a few first-stop touch points to provide individuals with easy access to mental health support and advice.

sections.label: NEHR enhancements review completion
sections.summary: MOH and IHiS reviewed the findings and most key NEHR enhancements are completed, with one further tentatively by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MOH and Integrated Health Information Systems (IHiS) have reviewed the findings and most of the key enhancements to NEHR have been completed, with one further to be completed tentatively by 2025.

sections.label: NEHR contribution, Health Information Bill timeline
sections.summary: MOH is working with CMS vendors, extending contribution incentives, and expects to introduce the Health Information Bill in the first half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have been working closely with the CMS vendors to improve their products and strengthen their backend services to support the GP clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We are bringing onboard more healthcare providers to contribute to the NEHR, by extending the Early Contribution Incentive scheme to GPs, private hospitals, radiological laboratories and clinical laboratories to support them in data contribution.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: With the Health Information Bill (HIB), it will become mandatory for them to contribute patients' data to NEHR.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We have been extensively consulting stakeholders such as our licensees and healthcare professionals, on issues surrounding data privacy and sharing, related to the HIB.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We had intended to table the HIB to Parliament sometime this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: But this is quite a very significant Bill and we felt more time is needed to engage our stakeholders and members of the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We thus expect to introduce the Bill in this House, in the first half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: I would also like to thank Mr Yip Hon Weng for raising the need to enable data sharing between the health and social sectors, this is indeed one of our aims under the HIB to support more integrated care and reduce administrative work, while ensuring data security.

sections.label: HealthHub viewing of NEHR records
sections.summary: Residents and authorised caregivers can view NEHR health information such as discharge summaries and selected test results via HealthHub.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For example, residents and their authorised caregivers can view health information from the NEHR, such as discharge summaries, selected blood test and radiology results, via HealthHub.

sections.label: Healthcare capacity and ageing priorities
sections.summary: Prioritises expanding healthcare capacity, including manpower, rolling out Healthier SG, and building an effective system for ageing in community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: What we will do is to prioritise the areas that we can make the most meaningful changes, where there is bang for the buck and focus on them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, we are focusing on expanding our healthcare capacity, which includes manpower, rolling out Healthier SG, and building up an effective system for ageing in community.

sections.label: Reviewing healthcare worker remuneration
sections.summary: Regularly reviews healthcare workers' remuneration to recognise their contribution and keep remuneration competitive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Part of this work, very importantly, is to regularly review remuneration of healthcare workers, to ensure that we recognise their contribution and to make sure that remuneration is competitive.

sections.label: Recruiting local and foreign healthcare workers
sections.summary: Actively recruits local and foreign healthcare workers to boost the workforce amid rising attrition from the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Of particular urgency now is to actively recruit both local and foreign healthcare workers to boost the workforce, given the rising attrition suffered in the last two years due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Healthcare workers applying for PR
sections.summary: More healthcare workers are hoped to come onboard in the second half of the year, and committed ones may apply for permanent residency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: They have so far been trickling into Singapore, but we hope in the second half of the year, more of them will start to come onboard.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And for those who have performed well and are committed to Singapore, we welcome them to apply for permanent residency (PR).

sections.label: Zero-tolerance policy against abuse
sections.summary: MOH announced a zero-tolerance policy against abuse and harassment of healthcare workers, to be translated into procedures and guidelines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As Members know, MOH has recently announced a zero-tolerance policy against abuse and harassment of healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And we intend to translate this to procedures and guidelines for all our healthcare institutions in the second half of this year.

sections.label: MediFund disbursement and top-up
sections.summary: MediFund disbursed $164 million in FY2021, not $100 million, and the Government topped it up by $1.5 billion in FY2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The MediFund disbursed $164 million in FY2021, not $100 million as stated by Mr Leong yesterday.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Government further topped up MediFund by $1.5 billion in FY2023.

sections.label: Government health expenditure growth
sections.summary: Nominal Government health expenditure tripled in the decade after 2010 and is expected to triple again by 2030, a nine-fold rise over 20 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the decade after 2010, our nominal Government health expenditure tripled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the following decade, that means up to 2030, it is expected to triple again.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, triple and triple – it means an increase by nine times over 20 years.

sections.label: Post-COVID length of stay
sections.summary: The crunch's main reason is average length of stay rising significantly within two years, raising utilisation by 15% post-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: I explained in this House before, I think it was during the White Paper debate on COVID-19, that the main reason for the crunch is that within a very short span of two years, you suddenly see average length of stay going up significantly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This means your utilisation has suddenly gone up by 15%, over two years, post-COVID-19.

sections.label: Major healthcare transformation
sections.summary: Post COVID-19, conditions and timing are right for a major healthcare transformation, with healthcare creating health in homes and communities beyond treating sickness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, post COVID-19 crisis, we have decided that the conditions and timing are right for us to effect a major healthcare transformation, building upon all the work that was done in previous years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Essentially, the idea is that healthcare needs to go beyond treating sickness in hospitals and clinics, but creating health in homes and communities.

sections.label: Population health system, Healthier SG
sections.summary: The population health system is being built through Healthier SG, mobilising family doctors and GPs for preventive care anchored in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, the population health system, which we are building up through Healthier SG, and we are mobilising all our family doctors and GPs to focus on preventive care that is anchored in the community.

sections.label: Aged care in community
sections.summary: Aged care in community, allowing people to leave well in a family environment surrounded by loved ones, is the next major healthcare area.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And if they wish, leave well in a family environment surrounded by their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, this aged care in community is the next major area of work in healthcare.

sections.label: Healthier SG community activities
sections.summary: Under Healthier SG, healthcare clusters will work with HPB, PA and SportSG to proliferate community physical activities and encourage resident participation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Indeed, when we consulted the public during Healthier SG, we heard from many residents that peer and family influence is a key factor in motivating them to adopt healthy life habits, such as regular exercise and to eat healthily.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, under Healthier SG, our healthcare clusters will work with community partners – HPB, PA, SportSG – to proliferate physical activities in the community and encourage strong participation by residents.

sections.label: Health habits and child development
sections.summary: Research findings show health habits inculcated from age three or four affect cognitive development, well-being and PSLE results later in life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Research findings now show good health habits, such as proper diet and use of devices, inculcated from as young as three or four years old, have a profound impact on the cognitive development and well-being of the child later on in life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And it actually does affect their PSLE results, based on our research findings.

sections.label: Green spaces and active living
sections.summary: MND and MOT have expanded green spaces, cycling paths and fitness corners islandwide, with plans for more Silver Zones and Green Man+ crossings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Over the years, MND and MOT colleagues have expanded green spaces, cycling paths and fitness corners islandwide to support active living.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: There are also plans to have more Silver Zones and Green Man+ at pedestrian crossings to allow our seniors to travel more safely and with confidence in their neighourhood.

sections.label: MPs and healthcare agenda
sections.summary: MPs including healthcare professionals, GPC Members, Labour MPs and NMPs, plus MOH political officeholders, will carry the healthcare agenda forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: On healthcare, there will be MPs who are healthcare professionals, Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) Members for Health, Labour MPs and NMPs, Members who feel strongly about healthcare who will carry the torch forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Most importantly, the MOH political officeholders will continue to put forth our agenda and address the concerns of our stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are all on the same side, trying to make the system better for Singaporeans.

sections.label: MediSave and MediShield Life reviews
sections.summary: MediSave and MediShield Life have been reviewed to ensure most Singaporeans and Permanent Residents can afford medical care in subsidised wards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MediSave and MediShield Life have been extensively and rigorously reviewed to ensure that the majority of Singaporeans and Permanent Residents can afford medical care when they opt for subsidised wards in restructured hospitals.

sections.label: Non-subsidised patients and market forces
sections.summary: Non-subsidised patients are those opting for A or B1 class, or foreigners, and the speaker thinks market forces determining costings are fair.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Patients who are not subsidised will be patients who opt in for A or B1 class, or foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, as a doctor, would think that allowing market forces to determine costings are fair.

sections.label: Public officers report to Government
sections.summary: Singapore has 150,000 public officers who report to the Government, not to any one political party.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore has 150,000 public officers who report to the Government, not to any one political party.

sections.label: Survival skills and leaders
sections.summary: The passage states that in war or apocalypse Singapore will need warriors, leaders and people with survival knowledge such as stopping bleeding and growing food.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Should war ever come to Singapore, should there be an apocalypse, we will need warriors, we will need leaders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I tell you, we will need people who know how to look after others, people who know how to stop bleeding, prevent infections, deliver babies, how to grow food, how to get clean water – any kind of knowledge to ensure that we survive.

sections.label: Recognising mental health issues
sections.summary: The passage calls for recognising mental health issues in yourself or your loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Recognise mental health issues in yourself or your loved ones.

sections.label: Overcoming barriers to surgery recovery
sections.summary: The passage states the surgery is simple in expert hands, but helping patients overcome emotional and mental barriers to seek health and recovery is the challenge.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The surgery itself is simple in expert hands.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is helping the patient to overcome all these other emotional and mental barriers to seek health and to eventually be on the road to recovery – that is the challenge for which I call for a global change and a whole-of-Government support.

sections.label: Cross-collaboration across sectors
sections.summary: The passage calls for cross-collaboration across Ministries, industries and the public-private divide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, cross-collaborate across Ministries, across industries, across the public-private divide.

sections.label: Procurement of chronic condition medicines
sections.summary: The passage states there is currently a procurement of all medications for chronic conditions for public medical institutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
sentences.text: In relation to the second question for the Government to procure all medicines, I understand that right now, there is a procurement for all medications for chronic conditions, for public medical institutions.

sections.label: Variegated healthcare and drug pricing
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's healthcare system is variegated unlike the nationalised NHS, and private doctors have different models including low consultation fees with drug margins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Ours is a variegated healthcare system, unlike, say, NHS, where everything is nationalised, all drug prices are more or less the same, centrally procured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And for private sector doctors, as Dr Tan Yia Swam said, they do have different models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There are doctors that charge very low consultation fees, but instead, they earn some margins by selling their drugs.

sections.label: Market forces and insurance structure
sections.summary: The passage states that in the private space, market forces may be allowed while discipline comes through structuring insurance and deciding what to subsidise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In the private space, sometimes, you want to let market forces operate, but, at the same time, have some discipline through how we structure insurance, what we subsidise, what we do not.

sections.label: Sobering health statistics
sections.summary: The passage lists health statistics including cancer, pneumonia, heart attacks, strokes, diabetes amputations, kidney failure, dementia, mental illness and osteoporosis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the current hot news is about the Cancer Drug List, I share a list of sobering health statistics: yearly, 26% of deaths are due to cancer; yearly, 20% of deaths are due to pneumonia; every day, 20 people die from heart attacks or strokes; every day, four people undergo leg amputations due to diabetes; Singapore ranks first in the world for diabetes-induced kidney failure; one in 10 people over 60 years old have dementia; one in 10 people have a mental illness; one-third of post-menopausal women have osteoporosis – and if they ever have a hip fracture, one in five will die within the year.

sections.label: Whole-of-Government healthcare effort
sections.summary: The passage states that healthcare must be a global, national whole-of-Government effort and not only a Ministry of Health effort.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Healthcare must be a global, national whole-of-Government effort and not only a Ministry of Health (MOH) effort.

sections.label: Regular salary revisions
sections.summary: The passage states that regular salary revisions to match inflation and the rising cost of living are essential.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Regular salary revisions to match inflation and the rising cost of living are essential.

sections.label: Three broad healthcare strategies
sections.summary: The passage states three broad strategies: identify and acknowledge problems, education at all levels, and cross-collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have explained why we need to support healthcare beyond the pandemic and why we need a whole-of-Government effort.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will now share three broad strategies on how this can be done: one, identify and acknowledge problems; two, education at all levels; and three, cross-collaboration.

sections.label: Night call for discharges
sections.summary: The passage recounts being called at night to identify patients fit for discharge because over 50 patients waited for a bed in the Emergency Department.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another story – once, when I was on call, I was called by my head of department in the middle of the night to urgently identify patients who may be fit for discharged in the morning, because there were 50-over patients waiting for a bed in the Emergency Department (ED).

sections.label: Long doctor working hours
sections.summary: A call can run from 8.00 am to 8.00 am the next day, followed by a full day's work until 6.00 pm, with 80 to 100 work hour weeks not unusual.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A call starts at 8.00 am and ends at 8.00 am the next day, followed by a full day's work until 6.00 pm the following day.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Eighty to 100 work hour weeks are not unusual.

sections.label: GP capitation and drug whitelist
sections.summary: Many doctors are concerned over the capitation model, the drug whitelist's impact and GP payments that may not cover running costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many doctors are concerned over the capitation model, about the impact of the drug whitelist and actual payments to general practitioners (GPs), which may not cover their running costs.

sections.label: Healthcare costs and financing complexity
sections.summary: Many people do not know treatment costs in Singapore and are stunned by the numbers, as healthcare financing is complex with many safety nets.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Not many people know the cost of treatments in Singapore and many are stunned when they first see the numbers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Healthcare financing is very complex and there are actually many safety nets for Singaporeans – public sector versus private sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Various combinations of co-payments and tiers of subsidies exist.

sections.label: Insurers working with healthcare providers
sections.summary: The speaker says this distracts from patient care work and repeats a March call for insurers to build closer relationships with healthcare providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It distracts from my real work in caring for patients.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is what I talked about in March, for insurers to build closer working relationships with healthcare providers so that patients have more assurance of affordability.

sections.label: Education for sustainable health
sections.summary: The speaker believes education from infancy through schooling and working years is key to good sustainable health, and cites studies on screen time harming brain development.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I firmly believe that education starting from as young as infancy and carrying on throughout our schooling and working adult years will be the key to good sustainable health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am glad that Minister Ong stated last month that MOH will partner MOE and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) to lay a strong foundation of health for our young.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Studies have shown that screen time adversely affects brain development.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Babies are not able to read faces as well and develop social skills, leading to later problems in executive and higher order functioning, such as the ability to focus, impulse control and emotional regulation.

sections.label: Pandemic vaccine hesitancy effects
sections.summary: During the pandemic, vaccine hesitancy and big pharma conspiracies had direct negative impacts on public health.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: During the pandemic, vaccine hesitancy and big pharma conspiracies had direct negative impacts on public health.

sections.label: Workplace health and insurance concerns
sections.summary: MOM should develop workplace health routines, affordable healthy food, exercise, flexi-hours, incentives, and work with MOH, CASE and MAS on insurance complaints.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), look into how to develop healthy routines at the workplace; ask the fitness industry; make affordable healthy foods easily accessible; encourage 10 to 20 minutes of simple office or chair-based exercises; get the bosses to implement such health practices; teach workers screen time limits and the value of mental breaks; look into flexi-hours so that they may prioritise time for themselves, family and medical appointments; consider incentives for good health; work with MOH, Consumer Association of Singapore, Monetary Authority of Singapore to look into alleged complaints of poorly paying corporate insurances and panel limitations imposed by TPAs; help workers to access good quality care.

sections.label: Sharing article across platforms
sections.summary: One good quality article with a good video might be shared across different Ministries and all social media platforms for wider reach.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One good quality article with a good video might be shared across different Ministries and across all the various social media platforms for wider reach.

sections.label: MSE food, labelling and urban farming
sections.summary: MSE's water and safe food mission may extend to affordable fresh produce; SFA regulates food safety labels, HPB nutrition labelling, and urban farming is rising.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE)'s mission to supply water and safe food may also extend to more affordable fresh produce, as eating whole foods has more health benefits than processed foods.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Food safety labels are regulated by the Singapore Food Agency (SFA), under MSE, but nutrition labelling is by HPB, under MOH.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is commendable is the rise of urban farming, supported by state agencies such as the Singapore Land Authority, Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA), Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority, SFA and Animal and Veterinary Service and Housing and Development Board (HDB).

sections.label: Patient cannot find operation histology
sections.summary: A patient tried to find her operation histology from HealthHub, Healthy 365 and Health Buddy but they could not find it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My patient tried to find her operation histology from HealthHub, Healthy 365 and Health Buddy; we could not find it.

sections.label: MTI, healthcare costs and concierges
sections.summary: MTI should look into rising local healthcare costs while maintaining Singapore's reputation, and the speaker is bothered by medical concierges collecting fees from providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) look into how this could contribute to increasing healthcare costs locally but still help Singapore maintain a leading-edge reputation as one of the best places to get good quality care?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am still deeply bothered by the businesses of medical concierges who collect fees from healthcare providers in exchange for bringing in foreigners for healthcare.

sections.label: Limited resources and gatekeeper question
sections.summary: The pandemic made everyone aware of limited resources like masks, test kits and oxygen, and asks who will be gatekeeper for those who need it most.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The pandemic has made everyone acutely aware of limited resources – masks, antigen rapid test kits, oxygen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are limited resources and who will be the gatekeeper as to who needs it most?

sections.label: Foreign nurse attrition rate
sections.summary: Singapore's foreign nurse attrition rate rose from 9.5% to 14.5% between 2019 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore experienced a significant attrition rate for foreign nurses, which increased from 9.5% to 14.5% between 2019 and 2022.

sections.label: Permanent residency for healthcare families
sections.summary: A proposal to grant permanent residency to immediate family members of good-performing healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Number one: granting permanent residency to the immediate family members of healthcare workers who are good performers.

sections.label: Nurse base salary increases
sections.summary: Singapore's public healthcare sector raised nurses' base salaries by 5% to 14% by 2022, with retention payments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's public healthcare sector has increased the base salaries of nurses by 5% to 14% by 2022 with retention payments as well.

sections.label: Preventing abuse of healthcare workers
sections.summary: The speaker states zero tolerance for abuse or threats and is encouraged by strides and Tripartite Workgroup recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There should be zero tolerance for abuse or threats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am encouraged by the great strides that we have taken in this area and with the recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup to Prevent Abuse and Harassment of Healthcare Workers.

sections.label: Caregiver-inclusive HR and eldercare leave
sections.summary: Suggestions include caregiver-inclusive HR practices, more eldercare leave, and attaching families to a medical social worker.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One low-lying fruit that we could consider is having more caregiver-inclusive HR work practices and granting more eldercare leave, a suggestion that has been raised before.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another is how we can work between Ministries to ensure that families who are already overwhelmed, can navigate the different caregiving options and available subsidies, ensuring that every family about to start this journey is attached to a medical social worker who can do a needs assessment and guide them along the way.

sections.label: Urgent dental care needs
sections.summary: Care may address urgent dental needs like painful cases and infections or swellings that can be life threatening.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The care may not need to encompass all dental care, like routine scaling and polishing but really to address the urgent needs, which means dental cases which can be very painful as well as cases with infection and swellings which, if untreated, can actually be life threatening.

sections.label: Nursing home dental access
sections.summary: Only some nursing homes have onsite dental services through Unity Denticare buses or volunteer mobile teams.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Out of all nursing homes in Singapore, only some have access to onsite dental services through Unity Denticare buses or mobile teams provided by volunteer groups or institutions.

sections.label: AIC care and dental support
sections.summary: AIC coordinates care for caregivers and seniors but excludes dental services, and volunteer services lack cost recovery, so the speaker calls for MOH and MSF support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) coordinates care for the caregivers and seniors but dental services are not included.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While we must commend the spirit of volunteerism as well, almost all these services do not have any cost-recovery component, making this model unsustainable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The cost of consumables, materials and manpower needs to be considered if services rendered are intended for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, to address these issues, I would like to call for more support from MOH and the MSF in helping different social service organisations develop their personalised dental capacities.

sections.label: Portable dental X-ray standard
sections.summary: They tried to make the handheld portable dental X-ray the standard of care for extractions in home-based settings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, we have tried to get the handheld portable dental X-ray as the standard of care for extractions done in home-based settings.

sections.label: HSEU and SMMWU membership strength
sections.summary: HSEU and SMMWU, representing nurses, allied health professionals and support staff, together have more than 35,000 members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For a start, I would like to share with this House that the Healthcare Services Employees Union (HSEU) and the Singapore Manual and Mercantile Workers' Union (SMMWU), which represent nurses, allied health professionals and support staff, collectively have a membership strength of more than 35,000 members.

sections.label: Independent observation of shift rosters
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to the Ministry to have a team independently observe the shift rosters assigned to healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
