sentences.text: Accordingly, I appeal to the Ministry to clearly have a team to independently observe the shift rosters that the healthcare workers are assigned.

sections.label: Intern received zero allowance
sections.summary: She was an intern at that same hospital in 2020 during her final year at Republic Polytechnic and received zero allowance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ironically, prior to that, she was an intern in that same hospital in 2020 during her final year of studies in Republic Polytechnic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I was shocked then to hear that she received zero allowance during her internship.

sections.label: Allowances for hospital interns
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Ministry or hospitals to review and grant allowances to students working in the real world, not free labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I do not think you will cripple the hospitals' or MOH's finances to grant an allowance to these students as they are working in the real world, not in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I call on the Ministry or hospitals to review this immediately and not make subject our students to free labour.

sections.label: Polyclinic appointment-only preference
sections.summary: Some people hoped polyclinics operate strictly on appointments as they still see many walk-ins when appointments are full.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on my interaction, some have highlighted that they hoped polyclinics operate strictly on appointments as they still see many walk-ins even when appointments are already full.

sections.label: Hospital shift hours and intern allowances
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to MOH to review shift working hours and calls on IHLs and MOH to disallow unpaid hospital internships as free labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amongst the challenges are long working hours for those on shift, fatigue from extended hours, demanding patients and caregivers, and a salary that should be reflective of the workload, not just during crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am appealing to MOH to seriously look into shift working hours at hospitals and not wait for an unwanted incident to take place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Another worrying area is students doing internships at hospitals who are not getting any allowances but are doing work similar to the staff, which can be classified as free labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I used to doubt such practices in the past when I heard about it, but reality hit me when my own daughter experienced it when she was did an internship at Sengkang Hospital in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I call on the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and MOH to review this practice and disallow this sort of free labour to be practiced in Singapore.

sections.label: Health and defence budget expenditure
sections.summary: Health's projected total expenditure of S$12.59 billion is second only to defence's S$13.41 billion in the 2023 national Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Looking at the 2023 national Budget that this House supported recently at the COS Sitting, health, with a projected total expenditure of S$12.59 billion is only second to defence, with a total projected expenditure of S$13.41 billion.

sections.label: GP renovation quotes and approval
sections.summary: After in-principle approval, the process to Temporary Occupation Permit takes six to 12 months, and a GP struggles with $200,000 renovation quotes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the in-principal approval came, we were told the process from concept drawing to Temporary Occupation Permit will take another six to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This GP is struggling with the capital renovation quotes of about $200,000 he has just received from potential contractors and he is thinking of giving up.

sections.label: Hospital emergency load and occupancy
sections.summary: The message shared that the hospital faced a very high emergency load with 100% occupancy in the past two weeks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The message shared that the hospital had been facing a very high emergency load, with 100% occupancy in the past two weeks.

sections.label: HR actions for healthcare workers
sections.summary: Calls for bolder HR actions, including employing above establishment in public hospitals, to allow surge buffer and rest for frontline healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the meantime, it will be important to step up bolder HR actions to support the frontline healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I repeat my suggestion for consideration of employing above establishment with the appropriate HR mechanism in public hospitals to allow buffer for surges and more importantly, essential rest for the physical and psychosocial wellness of our doctors, nurses and frontline healthcare workers.

sections.label: Nursing shortage and health empowerment
sections.summary: States constraints need Government trust, protocols or legislation and provider facilitation, and cites global, regional and Singapore nurse shortage figures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Both constraints require the trust and protocols or even legislation to be established by the Government, with the trust and facilitation from the private and public healthcare providers, including GP clinics as well as the not-for-profit charities providing community healthcare services, to empower more Singaporeans to receive the right knowledge of their health and take charge in managing our own health in an informed way with our care teams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Lest it becomes a motherhood statement, where we talk about but see people around us constantly losing their health with a heart attack or a sudden stroke, complications for chronic diseases as our population continues to age, let us have all hands on deck, in a clinically informed, administratively efficient and coordinated way, to ensure that this phrase is truth for most Singaporeans in the many years to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The chief executive officer of the International Council of Nurses (ICN) said last year that, "The scale of the worldwide nursing shortage is one of the greatest threats to health globally." The ICN estimates that due to existing nursing shortages, the ageing of the nursing workforce and the effect of COVID-19, up to 13 million nurses will be needed to fill the global nurse shortage gap in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Southeast Asia region alone is facing a shortfall of 1.9 million nurses, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore needs another 24,000 nurses, allied health professionals and support care staff to operate hospitals, clinics and eldercare centres by 2030.

sections.label: Ageing population and manpower share
sections.summary: States that staffing all health and social care institutions at ideal ratios would likely take a disproportionate share of Singapore's manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Considering our own ageing population in Singapore, which will require greater care needs, if we are to staff all our health and social care institutions with the doctors, nurses, allied health professionals and care workers to meet the ideal healthcare worker-to-patient ratios, the health and social care sector will likely take up a disproportionate share of Singapore's manpower and will starve other sectors of the economy of skills and talent.

sections.label: NEHR access and contribution rates
sections.summary: Cites a March 2023 Parliamentary reply that about 30% of licensed private ambulatory care institutions have NEHR view-access and under 4% contribute data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a Parliamentary Question reply by Minister Ong Ye Kung to Mr Leon Perera in March 2023, only about 30% of licensed private ambulatory care institutions have view-access to the NEHR and less than 4% are contributing data.

sections.label: Health Information Bill tabling
sections.summary: States the Health Information Bill was supposed to be tabled in Parliament in 2018 to make NEHR data contribution mandatory after a grace period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Health Information Bill was supposed to be tabled in Parliament in 2018 to make contribution of data to the NEHR mandatory for licensed healthcare groups after a grace period.

sections.label: NEHR comprehensive data and rollout
sections.summary: Cites Gan Kim Yong's 2017 remarks that comprehensive NEHR data requires every provider to contribute, and urges full rollout without undue delay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Former Minister for Health Gan Kim Yong said in 2017 that, "Patients can realise the full potential of the NEHR only if the data is comprehensive." He added that, "For NEHR data to be comprehensive, every provider and healthcare professional needs to contribute relevant data to it." Given the NEHR's goals and the fact that $660 million has been spent on the system so far, it is imperative that the full rollout is implemented without undue delay while addressing valid concerns from doctors.

sections.label: Private clinics IT systems challenge
sections.summary: Many private clinics find it a challenge to manage multiple IT systems and connect to CHAS, Healthier SG and the NEHR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Many private clinics find it a challenge to manage the dizzying array of IT systems that they need to manage in their clinics, connect to the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), Healthier SG and the NEHR.

sections.label: IT point of contact for GPs
sections.summary: A point of contact for IT matters lets GPs and clinic assistants focus on clinical care and stay current with technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By providing a point of contact for IT matters, GPs and their clinic assistants can then concentrate on delivering high quality clinical care to their patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This solution would not only enhance the efficiency and productivity of GPs but also help them stay current with the latest technological advancements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To boost productivity and augment manpower in the health and social care sector, we need to double down on the use of technology as a force multiplier and assist providers to implement and use these technologies.

sections.label: Government share of healthcare expenditure
sections.summary: The WHO reports the Government's share of healthcare expenditure rose from 33% in 2011 to 43% in 2019, below the OECD average of 75%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to the WHO, the share of healthcare expenditure covered by our Government has increased from 33% in 2011 to 43% in 2019, but this is still much lower than the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) average of 75%.

sections.label: MediShield and CareShield premiums estimate
sections.summary: In Budget 2021, an estimated $110,000 in MediShield and CareShield premiums would drain from parents' CPF savings for a family of four.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In my Budget 2021 speech, I estimated that the total MediShield and CareShield premiums paid by a family of four up to 65 years old for the parents and 25 years of age for two children will drain at least $110,000 from the parents' CPF savings, not including the loss in compound interest over the years – and that is at current premium levels.

sections.label: Funding MediShield and CareShield premiums
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to fund MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums for all Singapore Citizens, costing about $3 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, I repeat my call from the 2021 Budget Debate and urge the Government to fund MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums for all Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This will increase the Government's expenditure by about $3 billion a year, but this also means the CPF balances of Singaporeans will increase correspondingly by that amount.

sections.label: MediSave balances and withdrawals
sections.summary: As of 2020, MediSave Account holders had $110 billion in balances, but only $1 billion was withdrawn for direct medical expenses that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As of 2020, MediSave Account holders have accumulated $110 billion in balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, only $1 billion, or less than 1%, was withdrawn for direct medical expenses that year.

sections.label: MediFund and generation fund payouts
sections.summary: MediFund pays about $100 million yearly, while Pioneer and Merdeka Generation Funds pay out small shares of their balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, the MediFund only dishes out about $100 million a year, which only covers a paltry 0.4% of Singaporeans' total healthcare expenditure of about $25 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Since 2018, the Pioneer Generation Fund has a balance of about $7 billion but it only pays out about $400 million, or about 5% to 7% of its total assets each year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Medeka Generation Fund has a balance of about $6 billion but it only pays out about $200 million, or about 3% to 5% of its total assets each year.

sections.label: PSP drug procurement proposal
sections.summary: The PSP calls on the Government to centralise drug procurement across public and private medical institutions and distribute drugs not-for-profit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The PSP calls on the Government to centralise drug procurement across all public and private medical institutions and distribute drugs to public and private health facilities on a not-for-profit basis.
